meta.description: A policy problem-instrument map derived from Ohno's Learning to Industrialize and grounded in the public-action problem shelf. Eighteen root domains, their systems and concrete problems, and the instruments that answer them.

problems.name: Firm Domain
problems.statement: Domestic firms, especially SMEs, operate with low productivity and poor quality, limiting their ability to compete and upgrade.
problems.description: Weak firm-level capability is a root cause of failed industrial upgrading. SMEs lack management, technical, and quality control capabilities, and cannot absorb technology effectively.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: FDI–Local Firm Linkage Domain
problems.statement: Domestic supporting industries are too weak to supply core firms, and FDI operates in enclaves with few local linkages.
problems.description: Without supplier development and local absorptive capacity, FDI generates limited spillovers. Supporting industries are essential for clustering and value chain integration.
goals: Integrate local firms into value chains

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Industrial Human Resources Domain
problems.statement: There is a critical shortage of engineers, technicians, managers, and skilled workers needed for industrial upgrading.
problems.description: Industrialization requires a critical mass of capable people who can absorb, adapt, and create technology. TVET systems are disconnected from industry needs, and skill mismatch is widespread.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Industrial Finance
problems.statement: Firms, especially SMEs, cannot obtain adequate finance for equipment, technology, and working capital.
problems.description: Financial constraints prevent firms from upgrading. Collateral requirements, weak credit information, and lack of long-term finance are key obstacles.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Policy Process Domain
problems.statement: Government lacks the capability to design, implement, and adapt industrial policies suited to local conditions.
problems.description: Policy capacity includes diagnosis, dialogue with the private sector, learning from international experience, coordination across agencies, and implementation discipline.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 6-7). Routledge.

problems.name: Infrastructure Domain
problems.statement: Poor infrastructure, logistics, and administrative burden raise costs and reduce industrial competitiveness.
problems.description: Reliable power, transport, industrial parks, and efficient administration are necessary for industrial investment and cluster development.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Production Domain
problems.statement: Production is concentrated in low value-added activities and the structure does not shift: the economy does not move into higher-value, more complex activities.
problems.description: The production domain is the structure of what an economy makes and how: the mix of activities, their value added, complexity and linkages, and the process by which the structure changes over time.
goals: Raise the value added of production
Balance big projects with broad production support

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 1-2). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak SME Management and Technology Capability
problems.statement: SMEs lack management, technical, and quality control capabilities.
problems.description: SME upgrading is central to industrial deepening. Without it, domestic firms cannot supply MNCs or compete in export markets.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Poor Quality and Productivity
problems.statement: Firms produce low-quality goods with high defect rates and low productivity.
problems.description: Quality and productivity problems limit market access and upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Low Technology Absorption
problems.statement: Firms cannot absorb, adapt, and improve imported technology.
problems.description: Technology absorption requires technical skills, enterprise effort, and supporting institutions.
goals: Adapt foreign technology to local conditions

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 4-5). Routledge.

problems.name: Missing Supporting Industries
problems.statement: Domestic supporting industries are too weak to supply core firms.
problems.description: Supporting industries are essential for clustering and FDI linkage. Their absence raises import dependence and limits spillovers.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Local Suppliers Cannot Meet MNC Standards
problems.statement: Local firms cannot meet the quality, cost, and delivery standards of multinational buyers.
problems.description: This blocks FDI-local linkage and limits spillovers.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Linkage Programs
problems.statement: There are few effective programs to connect FDI with local firms.
problems.description: Linkage requires systematic matching, supplier development, and monitoring.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Low Local Absorptive Capacity
problems.statement: Local firms and workers cannot absorb knowledge transferred from FDI.
problems.description: Absorptive capacity depends on skills, management, and technology capability.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 3 and 5). Routledge.

problems.name: FDI Enclave Economy
problems.statement: FDI operates in enclaves with few links to the domestic economy.
problems.description: Without supplier development and local absorptive capacity, FDI generates limited spillovers.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Shortage of Engineers and Technicians
problems.statement: There are too few engineers and technicians for industrial upgrading.
problems.description: Engineering and technical skills are prerequisites for technology absorption and high-value production.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak TVET System
problems.statement: Technical and vocational education is disconnected from industry needs.
problems.description: TVET systems often lack equipment, qualified instructors, and industry participation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Shortage of Industrial Managers
problems.statement: Firms lack managers with industrial and quality management skills.
problems.description: Management capability is critical for productivity, quality, and technology adoption.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Skill Mismatch
problems.statement: Workers' skills do not match the needs of growing industries.
problems.description: Skill mismatch reduces productivity and increases unemployment among graduates.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 5). Routledge.

problems.name: Collateral Constraints
problems.statement: SMEs cannot provide sufficient collateral for bank loans.
problems.description: Collateral requirements exclude many viable SMEs from credit.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Credit Information
problems.statement: Banks lack reliable information to assess SME creditworthiness.
problems.description: Information asymmetry raises lending costs and reduces credit access.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Lack of Long-Term Industrial Finance
problems.statement: Firms cannot obtain long-term finance for capital investment.
problems.description: Long-term finance is needed for equipment, technology, and industrial upgrading.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: SME Finance Gap
problems.statement: SMEs face a persistent gap in access to affordable credit.
problems.description: SME finance gaps constrain upgrading and job creation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 4). Routledge.

problems.name: Random Policy Copying
problems.statement: Policies are copied from abroad without adaptation to local conditions.
problems.description: Policy copying without local diagnosis and ownership leads to poor implementation and weak results.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 6-7). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Coordination Across Agencies
problems.statement: Ministries and agencies pursue inconsistent industrial policies.
problems.description: Coordination failure causes duplication, inconsistent incentives, and weak implementation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Implementation Capacity
problems.statement: Policies are announced but not implemented effectively.
problems.description: Implementation requires administrative capacity, monitoring, and feedback.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 7). Routledge.

problems.name: Weak Public-Private Dialogue
problems.statement: Government and private sector do not communicate effectively on industrial policy.
problems.description: Without dialogue, policies may not address real constraints and firms may not support implementation.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Unreliable Power Supply
problems.statement: Firms face power outages and high energy costs.
problems.description: Unreliable power disrupts production and raises costs.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: High Logistics Costs
problems.statement: Poor transport and logistics raise export and input costs.
problems.description: High logistics costs reduce competitiveness and discourage investment.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Poor Industrial Parks
problems.statement: Industrial parks lack infrastructure, services, and effective management.
problems.description: Well-managed parks reduce investment costs and facilitate clustering.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Administrative Burden
problems.statement: Complex regulations and procedures raise costs and delay investment.
problems.description: Administrative burden discourages formal investment and firm growth.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 3). Routledge.

problems.name: Resource Dependence
problems.statement: The economy relies on natural resource rents rather than productive value creation.
problems.description: Resource dependence can weaken incentives for industrial learning and diversify poorly into manufacturing.
goals: Use resource revenues for industrial capability

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 1). Routledge.

problems.name: Aid Dependence
problems.statement: Development aid substitutes for domestic policy effort and private investment.
problems.description: Aid can help but may also create dependency if it does not build local capability and policy ownership.

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapter 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Big Project Bias
problems.statement: Policy favors large showcase projects over broad-based firm and skill development.
problems.description: Big projects can be politically attractive but may not generate widespread industrial learning or SME upgrading.
goals: Balance big projects with broad industrial support
Link large projects to local suppliers

references.label: Ohno, K. (2013). Learning to industrialize: From given growth to policy-aided value creation (Chapters 1 and 6). Routledge.

problems.name: Technical Research Human Capital Domain
problems.statement: The technical research system has too few researchers and scientists, and the careers, training and incentives that would produce and retain them are weak.
problems.description: The domain covers the human capital of technical research: the supply of researchers and scientists, the career structure that retains them, the research training that connects universities and industry, and the incentives that direct their work.

problems.name: Suboptimal Firm Size
problems.statement: Many firms operate below the minimum viable size, so support keeps them afloat without making them viable.
problems.description: Firm size is a threshold, not a continuum. Below the minimum viable size — the bundle of scale, capability, capital, demand access and coordination at which the firm reproduces itself — marginal support only postpones the choice between growth and consolidation. SME agencies often cannot separate a viability gap from a scale gap, and a portfolio-survival metric rewards keeping sub-scale firms alive instead of facilitating the merger that reaches the threshold.
goals: Diagnose the binding constraint on firm size
Facilitate consolidation to the minimum viable size
Condition support on a credible path to the threshold

references.label: An Essay on Firm Minimum Viable Size

problems.name: Shortage of Technical Researchers
problems.statement: Too few researchers and scientists to staff the technical research system and its institutes.
problems.description: The research system depends on a critical mass of researchers; below it, institutes cannot sustain programmes or train successors.

problems.name: Research Career Bottlenecks
problems.statement: Postdocs and researchers face few permanent positions — a pyramid structure that pushes talent out.
problems.description: A research career with no permanent rung above the postdoc is a threshold failure: the system trains more people than it can retain, and the surplus leaves.

problems.name: Weak Industry–Academia Research Training
problems.statement: Research training is disconnected from industry needs; programmes mix research with routine training.
problems.description: Training that is not aligned with industrial research demand produces credentials without absorptive capacity, and institutes that train but do not research.

problems.name: Short-Term Research Incentives
problems.statement: Funding cycles reward trendy topics over long-horizon work; bold and high-risk research is not rewarded.
problems.description: Incentives that reward short cycles and safe topics select against the long-horizon, high-risk work that technical research needs.

problems.name: Business Environment Domain
problems.statement: Firms face an administrative and regulatory environment that raises the cost of starting, operating and complying, and that discourages investment.
problems.description: The business environment is the set of rules, procedures and services a firm meets when it invests, operates and exits: business law, permits, inspections, and the one-stop services that reduce the administrative burden.

problems.name: Technical Research Domain
problems.statement: The technical research system is thin: institutes, programmes and industry links are too weak to generate and absorb technology.
problems.description: Technical research turns science into technique: the institutes, programmes, standards and industry links through which a country develops and absorbs technology.

problems.name: Scientific Research Domain
problems.statement: Fundamental science is underfunded and disconnected from the long horizon it needs.
problems.description: Scientific research is the creation of fundamental knowledge — the universities, laboratories and funding agencies whose output is the long-run input to technical research and innovation.

problems.name: Financial Domain
problems.statement: Firms cannot obtain the banking, capital-market and risk-finance services they need to invest and grow.
problems.description: The financial system intermediates savings into investment: banks, capital markets, development finance, guarantees and leasing.

problems.name: Monetary Domain
problems.statement: Monetary instability and a shallow monetary system raise the cost of contracting and deter long-term investment.
problems.description: The monetary system supplies the unit of account, the means of payment and the lender of last resort; its stability is a precondition for the rest of the financial system.
goals: Provide a lender of last resort

problems.name: Legal Domain
problems.statement: Property, contract and insolvency rules are too weak or too costly to enforce, so investment cannot be secured.
problems.description: The legal system makes investment enforceable: property rights, contracts, insolvency and the courts that adjudicate them.

problems.name: Labor Domain
problems.statement: The labor market does not match workers to firms: wages, informality and skills keep both sides from adjusting.
problems.description: The labor market prices and allocates work: employment, wages, informality, skills and the rules that govern hiring and separation.

problems.name: Public Governance Domain
problems.statement: Public administration lacks the capacity, coordination and accountability to deliver policy.
problems.description: Public governance is the administrative ecosystem: the civil service, the government-wide coordinating layer, the standards and the oversight through which the state delivers.

problems.name: Public Representation Domain
problems.statement: The representation system — who is authorized to speak for whom — is weakly designed, so preferences and accountability are poorly aggregated.
problems.description: Public representation is the design of the representative link: the electoral and parliamentary arrangements through which preferences are aggregated and the executive is held to account.

problems.name: Market Domain
problems.statement: Markets are not contestable: competition is weak, consumer protection is thin and market design is passive.
problems.description: Market policy is the design and policing of markets: competition, consumer protection, market design and the rules that keep markets contestable.

problems.name: Low Value-Added Activity Concentration
problems.statement: Production is concentrated in activities with little value added per worker and low complexity.
problems.description: A production structure specialised in assembly, raw processing or simple services captures little value per unit of output and leaves the economy exposed to cost competition.
goals: Raise the value added of output

problems.name: Lack of Structural Change
problems.statement: The structure of production does not shift toward higher-value activities; the economy stays in the same specialisation.
problems.description: Structural change is the movement of resources from lower- to higher-productivity activities. Without it, growth is extensive — more of the same — and the economy hits a ceiling.

problems.name: Weak Domestic Value Capture
problems.statement: Value is created in the country but captured elsewhere: assembly without design, brands, services or ownership.
problems.description: Participation in production does not equal capture of its value: the design, brands, distribution and finance that capture the margin often sit abroad, so the local economy keeps the low-margin step.
goals: Capture more of the value chain
Build domestic design, brands and services

problems.name: Narrow Production Base
problems.statement: The production base is narrow: too few activities and too little diversification to absorb shocks or sustain learning.
problems.description: A narrow base concentrates risk in a few activities and starves the economy of the variety from which new combinations and capabilities emerge.

problems.name: Low Productivity in Traditional Activities
problems.statement: Traditional and informal activities absorb most labour at low productivity, and they do not upgrade.
problems.description: Where most employment sits in low-productivity activities with no upgrading path, the aggregate productivity gap cannot close by moving a few workers into a modern enclave.

problems.name: Environmental System Domain
problems.statement: Environmental degradation and resource inefficiency constrain long-term production, and climate shocks repeatedly destroy productive assets.
problems.description: The environmental system is the ecological frame of production: resource efficiency, pollution, natural-resource governance and climate resilience.
goals: Protect productive assets from climate shocks
Govern natural resources for long-term wealth

problems.name: Fiscal Domain
problems.statement: The state cannot mobilize, allocate and manage public resources well enough to finance development or stabilize the economy.
problems.description: The fiscal system is how the state raises revenue, allocates the budget and manages its balance sheet over the cycle.
goals: Allocate public resources to productive uses
Keep the fiscal position stable across the cycle

instruments.name: Sovereign Wealth Fund

instruments.name: Diaspora Investment Fund

instruments.name: Project Preparation Facility

instruments.name: Syndicated Loan Facility

instruments.name: Blended Finance Facility

instruments.name: Export Incubator

instruments.name: Cluster Fund

instruments.mechanism: Pooled public and member contributions finance facilities, skills and market projects.

instruments.name: Cluster Marketing Program
instruments.description: A joint brand and promotion effort for the cluster.
instruments.mechanism: Members market under one identity at fairs, in catalogues and through shared channels.

instruments.name: Industrial Symbiosis Network
instruments.description: Firms exchange waste, heat, water and by-products.
instruments.mechanism: A broker matches streams between plants, turning disposal costs into inputs.

instruments.name: Cluster Skills Centre
instruments.description: Training tuned to the cluster's occupations.
instruments.mechanism: Employers and trainers co-design courses and share instructors and equipment.

instruments.name: Supplier Cluster Network

instruments.name: Cluster Observatory

instruments.mechanism: Regular data collection and analysis informs joint action and policy.

instruments.mechanism: Shared funding and governance sustain research on an industry problem.

instruments.mechanism: Cohorts receive capital, training and investor access in exchange for equity.

instruments.name: Duty Drawback Scheme
instruments.description: Refund of duties on imported inputs used in exports.
instruments.mechanism: Exporters recover border taxes, lowering the cost of competing abroad.

instruments.name: Set-Aside Program
instruments.description: A share of public contracts reserved for qualifying domestic firms.
instruments.mechanism: Procurement rules guarantee a market for targeted suppliers.

instruments.name: Cluster and Industrial Park Finance
instruments.description: Financing for industrial parks, zones and shared infrastructure.
instruments.mechanism: Dedicated capital lowers fixed costs and raises productivity inside the cluster.

instruments.name: Cluster and Supply-Chain Finance
instruments.description: Lending to interconnected firms across a value chain.
instruments.mechanism: Banks finance suppliers, machine-tool makers and logistics together, upgrading the chain as a whole.

instruments.name: Supply Chain Resilience Program
instruments.description: Redundancy and risk planning across supply chains.
instruments.mechanism: Firms map critical dependencies, qualify alternatives and hold strategic buffers.

instruments.name: Supplier Diversity Program
instruments.description: A buyer widens its supplier base to include new firms.
instruments.mechanism: Lead firms mentor and qualify additional suppliers, reducing concentration.

instruments.name: Inventory Management Program
instruments.description: Better inventory control across the chain.
instruments.mechanism: Shared demand data and replenishment rules reduce working capital and shortages.

instruments.name: Cluster Charter
instruments.description: A formal agreement among cluster actors on shared goals.
instruments.mechanism: Members sign a charter or memorandum defining roles, contributions and governance.

instruments.name: Thematic Working Group
instruments.description: A standing group focused on one cluster problem.
instruments.mechanism: Firms, agencies and researchers meet around a defined technical or market theme.

instruments.name: Additionality Testing
instruments.description: A counterfactual estimate of what private capital would have done.
instruments.mechanism: Analysts test whether public support changed behaviour before committing funds.

instruments.name: Cost per Outcome
instruments.description: A unit-cost measure of public support relative to results.
instruments.mechanism: Programmes report cost per verified outcome, making support comparable.

instruments.name: Composition Reporting
instruments.description: Disclosure of who actually receives public support.
instruments.mechanism: Beneficiary data are published by size, sector and location to expose capture.

instruments.name: Sunset Clauses
instruments.description: Automatic expiry of support unless renewed.
instruments.mechanism: A fixed end date forces periodic review and prevents permanent subsidies.

instruments.name: Prize Questions
instruments.description: Published challenges with rewards for solutions.
instruments.mechanism: Societies and agencies pose a precise question and award the best answer.

instruments.name: Tech-Scouting Mission
instruments.description: Missions that identify and bring back useful technologies.
instruments.mechanism: Scouts visit leading firms and labs, then report and broker adoption.

instruments.name: Scenario-Planning Workshop
instruments.description: Structured exercises exploring alternative futures.
instruments.mechanism: Participants build explicit probability ranges and corresponding strategy options.

instruments.name: Innovation Hub
instruments.description: A physical or organisational node where innovators meet.
instruments.mechanism: The hub co-locates firms, researchers and services around a theme.

instruments.name: Startup Ecosystem
instruments.description: A coordinated set of supports for new ventures.
instruments.mechanism: Incubation, capital, talent and markets are aligned around startup formation.

instruments.name: Applied Research Institute
instruments.description: Conducts applied research for firms and public missions.
instruments.mechanism: Institutes run contract research and shared laboratories that firms cannot build alone.

instruments.name: Research and Technology Organization
instruments.description: A not-for-profit applied research body serving industry.
instruments.mechanism: It bridges research and market with shared facilities, standards and engineers.

instruments.name: National Innovation Agency
instruments.description: The state body that funds and steers innovation.
instruments.mechanism: It runs grants, tax incentives, incubators and collaboration programmes under one mandate.

instruments.name: SME Development Agency
instruments.description: A dedicated agency for small and medium enterprise upgrading.
instruments.mechanism: It bundles finance, advisory, training and market access for SMEs.

instruments.name: Technology Commercialization Agency
instruments.description: Helps research results reach the market.
instruments.mechanism: It funds commercialization, brokers licensing and supports spin-offs.

instruments.name: Advanced Research Projects Agency
instruments.description: A mission agency funding high-risk, high-payoff technology.
instruments.mechanism: Program managers run stage-gated projects with aggressive timelines and technical authority.

instruments.name: Disruptive Innovation Agency
instruments.description: Fast, flexible funding for breakthrough commercialization.
instruments.mechanism: It uses rapid calls and milestones and tolerates failure to back radical ideas.

instruments.name: Corporate Research Laboratory
instruments.description: A company's central research lab for long-horizon work.
instruments.mechanism: It explores beyond products, publishing, patenting and spinning out ventures.

instruments.name: National Technology Mission
instruments.description: A coordinated national programme for one technology goal.
instruments.mechanism: It pools funding, laboratories and firms behind a measurable mission.

instruments.name: Research Data Repository
instruments.description: A public repository for research data and metadata.
instruments.mechanism: It mandates deposit and standardizes metadata so results are reusable.

instruments.name: Agricultural Innovation Program
instruments.description: Public funding for agri-food innovation.
instruments.mechanism: Grants and pilots support farm technology, processing and value chains.

instruments.name: Farm Science Centre
instruments.description: A local centre transferring farm technology to producers.
instruments.mechanism: It demonstrates practices, trains farmers and links them to research.

instruments.name: Digital Innovation Centre
instruments.description: A centre for digital technology adoption.
instruments.mechanism: It runs demonstrators, training and pilots for firms adopting digital production.

instruments.name: Technology Transfer Brokerage
instruments.description: Matches research supply with firm demand.
instruments.mechanism: Brokers scan patents, run matchmaking and negotiate licences.

instruments.name: Small Business Innovation Research Program
instruments.description: A competitive award funding SME research for public needs.
instruments.mechanism: Agencies set aside research funds; firms propose and keep the intellectual property.

instruments.name: National Productivity Organization
instruments.description: A national body driving productivity practice.
instruments.mechanism: It delivers diagnostics, training, standards and benchmarking to firms.

instruments.name: Trade and Investment Promotion Agency
instruments.description: Markets the country and supports its traders abroad.
instruments.mechanism: It runs overseas offices, missions, fairs and business matching.

instruments.name: High-Risk Research Program
instruments.description: Funding for early ideas with transformative potential.
instruments.mechanism: Peer review selects high-risk proposals with staged support and tolerance for failure.

instruments.name: Innovation Fund
instruments.description: A large flexible fund for innovation projects.
instruments.mechanism: It disburses by milestones, allows stacking and adapts to financing needs.

instruments.name: Stage-Gate Funding
instruments.description: Funding released in stages against technical gates.
instruments.mechanism: Each phase is reviewed; funding continues only when milestones are met.

instruments.name: Mission-Oriented Grant
instruments.description: A grant tied to a defined mission outcome.
instruments.mechanism: Funding is awarded against measurable mission targets rather than inputs.

instruments.name: Pre-Commercial Procurement
instruments.description: Public buyers purchase pre-market solutions.
instruments.mechanism: Procurement funds development of solutions that do not yet exist commercially.

instruments.name: Lead Customer Program
instruments.description: A public or corporate lead customer de-risks innovation.
instruments.mechanism: The buyer commits to early purchases, giving innovators a first market.

instruments.name: IP Brokerage Platform
instruments.description: A platform trading and licensing intellectual property.
instruments.mechanism: It lists rights, matches parties and standardizes terms.

instruments.name: Joint Development Agreement
instruments.description: Firms and research bodies co-develop a technology.
instruments.mechanism: Costs, intellectual property and milestones are shared under contract.

instruments.name: Precompetitive Research Consortium
instruments.description: Rivals jointly fund research below the market.
instruments.mechanism: Members share precompetitive results and standards.

instruments.name: State Holding Company
instruments.description: A state-owned company holding strategic assets.
instruments.mechanism: It manages portfolios, reinvests returns and executes state shareholdings.

instruments.name: State-Owned Enterprise Reform Program
instruments.description: Reforms state enterprises for performance.
instruments.mechanism: It professionalizes boards, sets targets and restructures loss-makers.

instruments.name: National Development Plan
instruments.description: A multi-year plan aligning budgets and reforms.
instruments.mechanism: It sets priorities, assigns agencies and tracks public investment.

instruments.name: Defence Offset Program
instruments.description: Defence purchases conditioned on industrial return.
instruments.mechanism: Contracts require local content, technology transfer or countertrade.

instruments.name: Local Assembly Program
instruments.description: Requires local assembly of imported technology.
instruments.mechanism: Licenses and tariffs reward firms that assemble and source locally.

instruments.name: Model Factory
instruments.description: A state factory demonstrating modern production.
instruments.mechanism: It trains workers and diffuses methods through imitation and transfer.

instruments.name: Chartered Trading Company
instruments.description: A state-chartered company with trade privileges.
instruments.mechanism: The charter grants monopoly or concession rights to build trade capacity.

instruments.name: High-Throughput Experimentation Facility
instruments.description: A facility running many experiments in parallel.
instruments.mechanism: Automation screens materials and processes far faster than laboratory work.

instruments.name: Regional Development Agency
instruments.description: A body coordinating development in a region.
instruments.mechanism: It assembles projects, funds infrastructure and aligns local actors.

instruments.name: Productivity Center
instruments.description: A local service centre that transfers productivity practice to firms.
instruments.mechanism: It runs diagnostics, training and demonstration for nearby SMEs.

instruments.name: Firm Education Center
instruments.description: A centre that educates firms, building the managerial and technical capabilities they need to upgrade.
instruments.mechanism: It delivers training, diagnosis and applied assistance so owners and managers can adopt better practice.

instruments.name: Firm R&D Capacity Program
instruments.description: A program that builds firms' in-house research and development capability.
instruments.mechanism: It funds R&D projects, equipment and researchers inside firms so they can absorb and generate technology.

instruments.name: Technology Transfer Subsidy
instruments.description: A subsidy that lowers the cost to firms of acquiring foreign technology.
instruments.mechanism: It offsets licensing, consultancy and adaptation costs so absorbed technology is cheaper than imported alternatives.

instruments.name: STEM Education Program
instruments.description: A funding program that expands science, technology, engineering and mathematics education.
instruments.mechanism: It funds places, curricula and teachers to build the technical workforce needed for technology absorption.

instruments.name: Master Artisan Program
instruments.description: A program that recognises and deploys master craftspeople to transmit practical skill.
instruments.mechanism: Master artisans train workers and anchor hands-on knowledge transfer in workshops and firms.

instruments.name: IP Licensing Reform
instruments.description: A reform that relaxes intellectual-property licensing conditions to widen access to protected technology.
instruments.mechanism: It uses waivers, compulsory licensing and flexible terms to let domestic firms use protected knowledge.

instruments.name: Technology Transfer Requirement
instruments.description: A condition that obliges an investor or licensee to transfer technology to local partners.
instruments.mechanism: It attaches transfer obligations to FDI approval, contracts or licences, making absorption a condition of market access.

instruments.name: Local Content Requirement
instruments.description: A rule that requires a specified share of inputs or value to be sourced locally.
instruments.mechanism: It mandates domestic sourcing in procurement, licensing and investment agreements to build local supplier capability.

instruments.name: Innovation Point System
instruments.description: A scoring scheme that awards points to SMEs for innovation activity and converts them into financing access.
instruments.mechanism: Points for R&D, patents and standards improve credit eligibility and lower the cost of loans.

instruments.name: Investor Information Portal
instruments.description: A portal that packages a location's investment conditions, incentives and procedures for investors.
instruments.mechanism: It publishes the data and contacts investors need to screen and enter a location, reducing search cost.

instruments.name: Investor Transparency Registry
instruments.description: A registry that discloses preferred investors, selection criteria and decision terms.
instruments.mechanism: Publication of who is sought and on what terms makes incentive negotiation visible and accountable.

instruments.name: Lead Agency Designation
instruments.description: The designation of a single lead ministry or agency accountable for a priority sector.
instruments.mechanism: One agency holds mandate, budget and coordination authority, cutting cross-agency fragmentation.

instruments.name: Talent Attraction Program
instruments.description: A program that recruits and retains skilled people from abroad and from the diaspora.
instruments.mechanism: It uses visas, incentives and placement services to bring scarce skills into the economy.

instruments.name: Business Linkage Program
instruments.description: A program that connects firms to buyers, partners and markets through matching and promotional events.
instruments.mechanism: It organises meetings, missions and linkages so firms find commercial partners.

instruments.name: Import Substitution Program
instruments.description: A program that replaces imported goods with domestic production.
instruments.mechanism: It protects or supports local producers of imported goods until domestic supply can compete.

instruments.name: FDI–Local Firm Integration Incentive
instruments.description: An incentive that rewards foreign investors for linkages with local firms.
instruments.mechanism: It ties benefits to sourcing, joint ventures or supplier development with domestic firms.

instruments.name: Cluster Quality Index
instruments.description: An index that ranks the quality and depth of economic activities within a cluster.
instruments.mechanism: It scores activities on capability, linkage and quality metrics to guide cluster policy.

instruments.name: Subcontracting Linkage Program
instruments.description: A program that facilitates subcontracting between large firms and SMEs.
instruments.mechanism: It publishes opportunities, brokers matches and certifies suppliers so small firms enter larger supply chains.

instruments.name: Leapfrogging Program
instruments.description: A program that targets a technological generation-skipping opportunity in a latecomer economy.
instruments.mechanism: It concentrates funding and missions on a new technology trajectory rather than incremental catch-up.

instruments.name: Supply–Demand Matching Laboratory
instruments.description: A laboratory that matches offers of goods and skills with demand from firms and buyers.
instruments.mechanism: It maps supply and demand and brokers matches, revealing the gaps that policy must fill.

instruments.name: Industry Association Support Program
instruments.description: A program that establishes and strengthens industry associations.
instruments.mechanism: It funds secretariats, training and representation so firms can act collectively.

instruments.name: Factory Rental Scheme
instruments.description: A scheme that rents ready-made factory space to local and foreign SMEs.
instruments.mechanism: It provides serviced premises at below-market rates so firms can start production without capital outlay on buildings.

instruments.name: Workforce Services Support Program
instruments.description: A program that supports recruitment, housing, commuting and healthcare for workers.
instruments.mechanism: It removes the non-wage obstacles that prevent firms from hiring and retaining workers.

instruments.name: Export Working Capital Facility
instruments.description: Short-term finance that funds production and shipment before export receipts arrive.
instruments.mechanism: It advances cash against orders or receivables so exporters can fulfil overseas contracts.

instruments.name: Export Loan
instruments.description: A bank loan earmarked for expanding export activity.
instruments.mechanism: It supplies credit to exporters for capacity, marketing and order fulfilment.

instruments.name: Firm Education Program
instruments.description: A program that educates firm owners and managers in the business, technical and organizational knowledge needed to run and upgrade an enterprise.
instruments.mechanism: It delivers courses, mentoring and practical training inside firms, building managerial and technical capability.
